terrain.surface: Gravel roads through Iowa countryside. Moderate elevation with rolling scenery.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: Iowa state championship. Rolling terrain with good access, low costs, and small field.

biased_opinion.summary: Iowa State Gravel TT Championship is a state championship in Iowa—rolling terrain with moderate elevation. The Iowa countryside is nice and it's good value, but the small field and limited national draw keep it in Tier 4.
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A solid Iowa state championship gravel race. Worth it for Iowa/Midwest riders. Not worth traveling for.

final_verdict.should_you_race: If you're local to Iowa—yes, it's solid. If you're traveling—skip it.
final_verdict.alternatives: For better Iowa races: Gravel Worlds, RAGBRAI.

logistics.food: Amana has full dining options. Stock nutrition.

editions.note: Held as part of the Millstream Gravel Cup weekend.

non_negotiables.why: Iowa rolling terrain requires sustained effort.

marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: State championship event with rolling terrain.

logistics.explanation: Registration and awards ceremony both happen at Millstream Brewery, creating a clear hub for race operations. Rick Hopson warns riders to check WeatherUnderground before equipment choices, suggesting basic course communication exists but riders need to do their own weather homework.

length.explanation: Elite riders like Nathan Kullbom finished in 58:44, with most category winners clocking 58-66 minutes total. Short even for a time trial format, though Rick Hopson describes the longer training version as 'brutal' with plenty of suffering packed in. More compact than Grinduro. As Water Crossings puts it: "A sharp left turn will lead you to a final water crossing that has an average depth of 1-2 feet… usually rideable, but as has been proven many times, not always."

technicality.explanation: The Abandoned Bridge features '25 yards of mud on the approach, 75 yards of mud on the other side, and a 12-inch concrete ledge on both ends.' The R.A.U.S. section includes 'sand dunes and water crossings that might require a bike hoist' according to course descriptions. Less technical than The Mid South. As Rick Hopson puts it: "The IC-Amana-IC loop, a 70-ish mile chip, gravel, B-road, mud, and water-soaked route from IC to Amana, with a stop at the Millstream Brewery, and then back."

elevation.explanation: Course description mentions 'a gentle rise followed by a distinct climb' with three hills that are 'all big ring-able, but all attention-getting.' The False Flat finish section adds some vertical interest but nothing approaching serious climbing terrain. Less climbing than The Mid South.

climate.explanation: Race day 2015 saw 'clear, 87 degrees, wind 12 mph' conditions. Rick Hopson notes that road shoes only work 'if it has rained in the past week,' indicating weather significantly affects course conditions and equipment choices. More weather exposure than Belgian Waffle Ride San Diego. As Rick Hopson puts it: "A visit to WeatherUnderground might be in order, but regardless, only Lobster will be sporting road shoes for this event if it has rained in the past week."

altitude.explanation: Iowa river bottom terrain near Amana sits at minimal elevation. Altitude isn't mentioned in any rider reports or course descriptions because it's not a factor in this low-elevation Midwest location. Lower altitude than Gravel Worlds — no thin-air concerns.

adventure.explanation: Amana, Iowa is famous for German heritage tourism, not gravel racing adventure. Forty miles of flat farm roads in a time trial format eliminates exploration, suffering, and discovery. This is suburban training ride distance with a timer attached, not an adventure worth traveling for. As The Abandoned Bridge puts it: "This is the first of the Three Challenges: the Abandoned Bridge, a lost and ancient iron span that somehow remains on this gravel road from an old route over the Iowa River, now impassable to all but ..."

prestige.explanation: It's a state championship with 'TT' in the name, which sounds official until you realize Iowa isn't the epicenter of gravel racing. No pro riders show up, no media coverage exists, and the gravel community doesn't discuss it online. The $20 entry fee tells you everything about how seriously the cycling world takes this event.

race_quality.explanation: Course features three distinct challenges including the abandoned iron bridge and R.A.U.S. sand section. The final 1.3 miles vary from 'smooth and hard packed dirt' to 'deeply rutted and completely unridable goo' depending on recent rainfall. As Post-Race Location puts it: "Award ceremony to be held at Millstream Brewery immediately following conclusion of event. Awards will be in the form of trophies and state championship medals."

experience.explanation: Rick Hopson describes the IC-Amana-IC loop as a 70-mile gravel time trial featuring the Abandoned Bridge with its 25 yards of approach mud, the R.A.U.S. sand dunes and water crossings, and a False Flat B finish that ranges from smooth hardpack to unridable goo. The beer stop at Millstream Brewery mid-route and post-race camaraderie define this as a local cycling club tradition more than a polished event.

community.explanation: Awards ceremony happens at Millstream Brewery immediately after racing. The event sometimes coincides with the Festival of Iowa Beers, capped at 1,200 people, creating a proper post-race celebration atmosphere with local brewery integration.

field_depth.explanation: With a field of 50-100 riders, elite category winner Nathan Kullbom suggests some competitive depth exists. However, the race primarily serves to share a local training route with a broader audience rather than attract serious regional or national-level gravel talent. Thinner field than Ouray Gravel Grinder.

value.explanation: Twenty-dollar entry includes state championship medals, trophies, and post-race ceremony at Millstream Brewery. When the race coincides with Festival of Iowa Beers, riders get access to Iowa brewery tastings as part of the broader event experience.

expenses.explanation: The $20 entry is nearly free money, but Amana, Iowa isn't a destination with cheap flights or abundant lodging. You'll drive there, which keeps costs reasonable if you're regional. No information on parking fees or hidden costs, but at this scale, they're probably just happy you showed up. Similar expense level to Belgian Waffle Ride San Diego.
